**Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity reflects smartphone social activity** (URL: [https://www.cell.com/iscience/fulltext/S2589-0042(21)00465-X](https://www.cell.com/iscience/fulltext/S2589-0042\(21\)00465-X))

 *(Published May 2021\)*

\*Note on this study: focuses on general online social activity, not just social media (messenger apps are major focus). Reason I included this in research is for link between social activity online and dopamine, since social media is clearly a form of social activity (although the extent, for example scrolling vs. interacting w/ other users in chat, varies person-to-person and app-to-app). Will look into further studies on social media specifically after this.

* Authors note that striatal dopamine tone, which is the level of dopamine activity in the striatum, “has been linked with increasing vigor … and regulating behavioral variability … as a function of reward context”  
* Study aimed to establish link between dopamine function in users’ brains and smartphone social interactions, given links between dopamine function and real-life social interaction, and also [speculation](https://www.iomcworld.org/open-access/neurotransmitter-dopamine-da-and-its-role-in-the-development-of-social-media-addiction-59222.html) (reference provided in study) about dopamine’s relationship to social media use  
  * In layman’s terms, examined whether differences in users’ brains would correlate to differences in social media use  
* Participants were “healthy, young adults in the Radboud University community,” with 27 individuals agreeing to participate and the final sample size being 22 students aged 18 to 33  
  * Major shortcoming of this study is small sample size, but researchers did track significant amount of social app use over time for each of these individuals which increases reliability of results  
    * Provides good starting point to begin establishing SM use-dopamine connection, and for further research

    

* At the beginning of study, participants completed a PET scan measuring striatal dopamine synthesis capacity   
* Over the course of multiple weeks (median of 32 days, with the 10th percentile being 26 days and the 90th being 50 days), researchers tracked participants’ touchscreen logs on their smartphones to measure overall usage in interactions/day and proportion of interactions on social apps  
* **Found** a reliable “negative relationship between the proportion of social interactions and dopamine synthesis capacity … in bilateral posterior putamen,” showing **an association between individual differences in the proportion of interactions on social apps and those individuals’ dopamine synthesis capacity in the bilateral posterior putamen**:  
  ![][image1]  
* Using measurements from other apps on phone (such as the Notes app), researchers controlled for typing, age, and gender factors that could also help explain the relationship. However, social interactions were found to track between-subjects variance in dopamine synthesis more effectively

* Concluded that **there is a “strong and focal relationship between dopamine synthesis capacity in the bilateral posterior putamen and smartphone social app use**, which is also **specific to social app use**.”  
* The authors also claim that this **“informs speculations” about social digital behavior’s relationship to dopamine**, including social media app use  
* They do **note that some other behavioral addictions**, such as gambling, **have been associated with higher dopamine synthesis capacity rather than lower** dopamine synthesis capacity, so they believe that “**dopamine synthesis capacity may interact with other factors in** conferring risk for **problematic social media use**”   
  * D2 receptor density is one factor they consider
